problem:
Problem description
- There are $$m$$ production points indexed by $$i \in \mathcal{I}$$, $$n$$ demand points indexed by $$j \in \mathcal{J}$$, and $$p$$ intermediate marshaling stations indexed by $$k \in \mathcal{K}$$.
- Each production point $$i$$ has available supply $$a_i$$.
- Each demand point $$j$$ has required demand $$b_j$$.
- Each marshaling station $$k$$ has a fixed usage cost $$f_k$$ and a maximum transshipment capacity $$q_k$$.
- The unit transportation cost from production point $$i$$ to marshaling station $$k$$ is $$c_{ik}$$, and the unit transportation cost from marshaling station $$k$$ to demand point $$j$$ is $$c'_{kj}$$.
- The instance is assumed to have total available supply at least as large as total demand.
- The planning goal is to choose shipment quantities and station-usage decisions so that all demand is satisfied at minimum total cost.
- All material must be routed from production points to demand points through intermediate marshaling stations; direct shipment from a production point to a demand point is not allowed.
- Every demand point must receive its full required quantity.
- Shipments leaving any production point cannot exceed that point’s available supply.
- If a marshaling station is used, the total amount transshipped through it cannot exceed its capacity.
- If a marshaling station is not used, no material may pass through it and no fixed usage cost is incurred.
- Flow entering a marshaling station must be matched by flow leaving that station so that material is conserved at the station.
- A solution is represented by:
  - $$x_{ik}$$, the quantity shipped from production point $$i$$ to marshaling station $$k$$.
  - $$y_{kj}$$, the quantity shipped from marshaling station $$k$$ to demand point $$j$$.
  - $$z_k$$, a binary indicator showing whether marshaling station $$k$$ is used.
  - $$Z$$, the total transportation-and-usage cost of the plan.

Input Format
{
  "m": "integer $$m$$, number of production points",
  "n": "integer $$n$$, number of demand points",
  "p": "integer $$p$$, number of marshaling stations",
  "supply": "array of length $$m$$, where $$supply[i] = a_i$$ is the available supply at production point $$i$$",
  "demand": "array of length $$n$$, where $$demand[j] = b_j$$ is the required demand at demand point $$j$$",
  "fixed_cost": "array of length $$p$$, where $$fixed\_cost[k] = f_k$$ is the fixed usage cost of marshaling station $$k$$",
  "capacity": "array of length $$p$$, where $$capacity[k] = q_k$$ is the maximum transshipment capacity of marshaling station $$k$$",
  "cost_production_to_station": "matrix of shape $$m \times p$$, where entry $$c_{ik}$$ is the unit cost from production point $$i$$ to marshaling station $$k$$",
  "cost_station_to_demand": "matrix of shape $$p \times n$$, where entry $$c'_{kj}$$ is the unit cost from marshaling station $$k$$ to demand point $$j$$"
}

Output Format
{
  "station_used": "binary array of length $$p$$, where $$station\_used[k] = z_k$$ indicates whether marshaling station $$k$$ is used",
  "shipments_to_station": "nonnegative matrix of shape $$m \times p$$, where entry $$x_{ik}$$ is the shipment from production point $$i$$ to marshaling station $$k$$",
  "shipments_to_demand": "nonnegative matrix of shape $$p \times n$$, where entry $$y_{kj}$$ is the shipment from marshaling station $$k$$ to demand point $$j$$",
  "total_cost": "scalar value $$Z$$ giving the minimum total cost of the transportation plan"
}

Example(s)

Input 1
{
  "m": 2,
  "n": 2,
  "p": 2,
  "supply": [100, 150],
  "demand": [80, 120],
  "fixed_cost": [10, 15],
  "capacity": [100, 100],
  "cost_production_to_station": [[2, 3], [4, 1]],
  "cost_station_to_demand": [[3, 2], [1, 4]]
}

parameters.name: m
parameters.description: Integer count of production points; the set of production points is \mathcal{I} = {0,\dots,m-1}

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Integer count of demand points; the set of demand points is \mathcal{J} = {0,\dots,n-1}

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: Integer count of marshaling stations; the set of stations is \mathcal{K} = {0,\dots,p-1}

parameters.name: supply
parameters.description: Available supply at each production point i \in \mathcal{I}

parameters.name: demand
parameters.description: Required demand at each demand point j \in \mathcal{J}

parameters.name: fixed_cost
parameters.description: Fixed usage cost of each marshaling station k \in \mathcal{K}

parameters.name: capacity
parameters.description: Maximum transshipment capacity of each marshaling station k \in \mathcal{K}

parameters.name: cost_production_to_station
parameters.description: Unit shipping cost from production point i \in \mathcal{I} to marshaling station k \in \mathcal{K}

parameters.name: cost_station_to_demand
parameters.description: Unit shipping cost from marshaling station k \in \mathcal{K} to demand point j \in \mathcal{J}

variables.name: shipments_to_station
variables.description: Quantity shipped from production point i \in \mathcal{I} to marshaling station k \in \mathcal{K}

variables.name: shipments_to_demand
variables.description: Quantity shipped from marshaling station k \in \mathcal{K} to demand point j \in \mathcal{J}

variables.name: station_used
variables.description: Binary indicator equal to 1 if marshaling station k \in \mathcal{K} is used, and 0 otherwise

constraints.name: demand_satisfaction
constraints.description: Each demand point must receive exactly its required demand through marshaling stations

constraints.name: supply_limit
constraints.description: Total shipment leaving each production point cannot exceed its available supply

constraints.name: station_capacity_usage
constraints.description: If a station is used, total flow through it is limited by its capacity; if it is not used, no flow may pass through it

constraints.name: station_flow_conservation
constraints.description: Removed because station balance is now embedded in the station capacity/usage constraint
constraints.formula: inflow equals outflow at each station

constraints.name: no_direct_shipping
constraints.description: Removed because direct production-to-demand shipping is structurally excluded by the variable set; no separate algebraic constraint is needed
constraints.formula: no direct production to demand shipment

constraints.name: nonnegative_shipments
constraints.formula: x_{ik} \ge 0 \; \forall i\in\{0,\dots,m-1\},\forall k\in\{0,\dots,p-1\},\qquad y_{kj} \ge 0 \; \forall k\in\{0,\dots,p-1\},\forall j\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}

constraints.name: binary_station_usage
constraints.description: Station usage indicator must be binary

objectives.name: total_cost_minimization
objectives.description: Minimize the total transportation cost on both shipment legs plus fixed usage costs for activated marshaling stations

final_objective.description: Minimize the total transportation cost on both shipment legs plus fixed usage costs for activated marshaling stations.
